newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady to lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady to lower on weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady to softer Wednesday as a lack of weather-related demand kept most buyers away from the market.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain above-normal through Friday but then moderate to near-normal levels for the weekend as a cold front moves toward the East Coast.

Firm, peak power prices into the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Thursday were mostly steady in the $14.00-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Tuesday's tighter range of $15.00-16.00.
Firm, off-peak power into TVA was still talked at $13.50-14.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery ranged from $20.00 to $21.00, down $1-2 from Tuesday's levels.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $14.00 per MWh.
Florida Power and Light's 839 megawatt St Lucie 2 nuclear power unit remained at 90 percent power for inspections, but most traders agreed the power reduction was not impacting the market.

Despite the softening in the southern Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) prices, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast pipes regained more than five cents to the low-$3 per million British thermal units area.
